title: Regulatory Intake Harmonizer — unified triage for DPA / HIPAA / GDPR and vendor questionnaires
creator: Amrita Singh
description: Problem: Enterprise sales and customer success receive a high volume of requests that reference overlapping regulatory and contractual needs (DPA clauses, GDPR data residency, HIPAA controls, SOC2 evidence, and vendor questionnaires). Current intake is manual, inconsistent, and creates long SLAs to respond. Goal: build a lightweight, deterministic intake orchestrator ("Harmonizer") that standardizes metadata collection, applies a transparent risk/scoring heuristic, and routes requests to the correct queue (SRE/Security/Legal/Compliance/Engineering) with suggested SLAs and remediation steps. Deliver a minimal viable flow that reduces manual classification time by >=50% and clarifies TTR expectations for customers and AE/CS teams.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Intake form with enforced required fields (data types affected, jurisdiction, customer tier, requested deliverable) is published and linked from CS/AEs. 2) Automated tagger classifies >=85% of incoming items into one of: DPA, GDPR, HIPAA, SOC2, VendorQuestionnaire, Other. 3) Risk score computed deterministically (0-100) and routing rules map score ranges to queues and SLA tiers. 4) For high-risk (>75) items, auto-escalate to Legal + Security with a prepopulated PRD and evidence checklist. 5) Dashboard shows TTR by tier, classification accuracy, and queued items. 6) Playbook published for AE/CS including example responses and temporary mitigations.
approach: 1) Intake form: collaborate with CS to design a concise form (max 10 fields) capturing customer, product impacted, data category matrix, jurisdiction, deadline, and requested artifact. 2) Deterministic scoring: build rule-based heuristic combining data sensitivity (weights for PHI, PII), contractual ask complexity (contract language / deliverable type), jurisdictional severity (EU/UK/HIPAA states), and customer tier multiplier. 3) ML classifier: seed with 1,200 labeled historical inbound emails & questionnaires to build a light classifier to supplement the rule engine; keep ML as advisory for first iteration. 4) Routing policies: implement in Console routing layer to send items to Security Intake queue, Legal, or Engineering based on score thresholds; provide auto-fallbacks that assign to 'Intake Triage' when confidence < 0.6. 5) Observability: add a per-item trace including the scoring breakdown so reviewers can see why an item routed the way it did. 6) Run a 4-week pilot with AE/CS and two customer accounts (one enterprise in EU, one HIPAA-regulated US) to validate thresholds.
out_of_scope: Full automation of vendor questionnaire completion (we will supply suggested answers and evidence bundles but not complete responses automatically). Running a SOC2 or ISO certification — only evidence mapping and guidance is in scope.

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overconfidence in ML could misroute escalations and cause legal exposure. Mitigation: ML advisory only; all high-risk auto-escalations include required human approval before legal action. Risk: Poor adoption by AEs if form is too long. Mitigation: Co-design with top 8 AEs and implement canned message templates in CRM. Risk: Score tuning may bias against certain regions. Mitigation: Pilot with EU and US HIPAA accounts and measure false negative rate by jurisdiction.
notes_for_engineering: Provide a webhook endpoint that accepts intake JSON (max 10 fields) and returns a deterministic score + routing decision. Expose scoring breakdown in response. Provide a feature flag to enable 'auto-escalate' for pilot customers. Instrument metrics: classification confidence, route latency, time-to-assignment.
implementation_plan: Week 1: finalize form and scoring rules; build prototype spreadsheet and run retrospective labeling. Week 2: eng implements webhook + Console routing UI. Week 3: integrate Security and Legal playbooks and evidence templates; enable pilot for 2 accounts. Week 4: measure metrics, collect feedback, iterate and publish final playbook. Post-pilot: extend to full AE organization and add ML advisory calibration.
follow_up_tasks: 1) Label 1,200 historical intake items (owner: Jordan) 2) Legal to publish clause templates and evidence checklist (owner: Priya) 3) Engineering to deliver webhook and routing integration behind a feature flag (owner: Kenji) 4) CS to identify pilot customers and coordinate communication (owner: Mark Dobson)
expected_metrics: - 50% reduction in manual triage time per item; - Classification accuracy >=85% for primary category at week 4; - Mean time-to-assignment for high-risk items < 4 hours; - Pilot CS satisfaction >=8/10
communication_plan: Publish pilot playbook in Confluence, announce in #cs-intake and #security channels, run a 30-minute walkthrough with AE leads, and surface initial dashboards to weekly GTM sync.
legal_impact_summary: Where customer asks require contractual change (DPA clauses) route to Legal with prefilled template and impact estimate. For HIPAA and high PHI requests, include KMS/HSM and logging requirements in the evidence checklist. Legal to own final acceptance and approvals.
decision_log: 2025-02-14: Chose rule-based scoring for MVP instead of end-to-end automation. 2025-02-27: ML will run in shadow mode for evaluation. 2025-02-24: Acceptance updated to require evidence checklist prepopulation for common asks.
visibility: AE/CS pilot, Security, Legal, Platform Engineering, Product. Dashboard access will be provided to Security and AE leads during pilot.
